Stewart, Calculus: Early Transcendentals · Section 15.7 · Exercise 54

The Average Value of a Function over a Paraboloid Cap

Problem

The average value of a function f(x,y,z) over a solid region E is

fave​=V(E)1​∭E​f(x,y,z)dV,

where V(E) is the volume of E. Find the average value of f(x,y,z)=x2z+y2z over the region enclosed by the paraboloid z=1−x2−y2 and the plane z=0.

Reading the solid

The paraboloid opens downward from its vertex (0,0,1). The two surfaces meet on the rim where both equations hold, that is, where 1−x2−y2=0. This equation describes the unit circle x2+y2=1. The solid therefore projects onto the unit disk

D={(x,y):x2+y2≤1}.

Fix a point (x,y) in D. The vertical line through that point enters E on the floor z=0 and leaves E on the paraboloid. The solid is the set of points between these two surfaces:

E={(x,y,z):x2+y2≤1, 0≤z≤1−x2−y2}.

Introduce polar coordinates in the xy-plane, x=rcosθ and y=rsinθ, so that x2+y2=r2. A small polar rectangle has area rdrdθ, hence the volume element is

dV=dzrdrdθ=rdzdrdθ.

In these coordinates the cap has constant bounds in two of the three variables:

0≤z≤1−r2,0≤r≤1,0≤θ≤2π.

Solution

Step 1 — Compute the volume V(E)

The denominator of the average value is the volume of the cap. Integrate the volume element over the three ranges of the polar description:

V(E)=∫02π​∫01​∫01−r2​rdzdrdθ=∫02π​∫01​r(1−r2)drdθ.

The radial integral is elementary:

∫01​(r−r3)dr=[2r2​−4r4​]01​=21​−41​=41​.

The result does not depend on θ, so the outer integral multiplies it by 2π:

V(E)=2π⋅41​=2π​≈1.5708.

Step 2 — Simplify the integrand

Both terms of f carry the factor z, and the two squared terms add to x2+y2=r2:

f(x,y,z)=x2z+y2z=(x2+y2)z=r2z.

This step matters: after the substitution the integrand no longer contains x or y separately, so no trigonometric term survives the integration.

Step 3 — Integrate f over the cap

Multiply the integrand by the volume element and integrate in the order z, then r, then θ:

∭E​(x2+y2)zdV=∫02π​∫01​∫01−r2​r2z⋅rdzdrdθ.

With respect to z, the factor r3 is constant:

∫01−r2​r3zdz=r3[2z2​]01−r2​=2r3(1−r2)2​=21​(r3−2r5+r7).

Integrate this polynomial over 0≤r≤1:

∫01​21​(r3−2r5+r7)dr=21​(41​−62​+81​)=21​⋅241​=481​.

The outer integral adds the factor 2π:

∭E​(x2+y2)zdV=2π⋅481​=24π​≈0.1309.

Step 4 — Divide by the volume

Insert the two results into the definition of the average value:

fave​=V(E)1​∭E​fdV=π/2π/24​=24π​⋅π2​=121​≈0.0833.

The two factors of π cancel, so the average value is a rational number even though both the volume and the integral contain π. The value is small because f vanishes on the rim and stays small near the axis, where the cap is high but r2 is small.

Answer

fave​=121​≈0.0833.

Notation

SymbolMeaning
fave​The average value of the function f over the solid E, that is, the integral of f divided by the volume of E.
V(E)The volume of the solid region E, in cubic units.
∭E​fdVThe triple integral of f over E; it is the limit of sums of f times small volumes.
dVThe volume element. In Cartesian coordinates dV=dxdydz; in the polar coordinates used here dV=rdzdrdθ.
EThe solid region of integration, here the cap between the paraboloid and the plane z=0.
DThe projection of E onto the xy-plane, here the unit disk.
z=1−x2−y2A downward paraboloid with vertex (0,0,1); it is the upper boundary of E.
r,θPolar coordinates in the xy-plane: r is the distance from the z-axis and θ is the angle in the plane.
the factor rThe Jacobian factor of polar coordinates. A small polar rectangle has area rdrdθ, not drdθ.
πThe ratio of a circle's circumference to its diameter, π≈3.14159.

Verification

Three scripts check the result; each one runs from inside calculus-15.7.54/solution.

  • part1_step1.py confirms the projection disk, tabulates the cap height 1−r2, and estimates the average value by Monte Carlo sampling of four million points. The estimate is 0.08341 with standard error 0.00005, that is 1.5 standard errors from 1/12.
  • part1_step2.py repeats the whole computation with SymPy and returns V(E)=π/2, ∭E​fdV=π/24, and fave​=1/12.
  • part1_step3.py evaluates the integral with mpmath in polar order and in Cartesian order. Both values agree with π/24 to fifteen digits, and the quotient with the volume reproduces 0.0833333333333.
